summary: Fake PSA slabs were the biggest collector story. Posts on how to spot counterfeit slabs got the most reach of the day, and trust in buying graded cards on open marketplaces is shaky. GameStop added luxury watches to Power Packs, and Rolex pull posts went viral, which puts a mainstream rival right into the watches category we already have. Other pack products kept growing too: PrizePicks packs, Tilt Rips $1 packs, Disney Pinnacle x NFL pin packs and live breaks on BOXED. Solflare Packs talk was steady and positive, led by how-to threads, but it still comes mostly from small community accounts.

sources_note: X search via the x connector, posts from 2026-10-29 09:00 UTC to 2026-10-30 09:00 UTC, 10 post searches plus 1 X news search. Engagement numbers are copied from the X API at scan time. The GameStop watches, Dragonite and McDonald's items come from X news summaries (Grok-written), not confirmed reports. The PrizePicks $2.8M pull is a third-party recap claim. Payments talk was thin: card, Apple Pay and Google Pay searches returned mostly carding spam, which was skipped; the Philippines card-only drop rule is the one real payments signal. One Solflare Packs mention (@iamjamalubah) uses expected-value and buyback wording, which is investment-style framing we should not echo. @vision_harry's post points to a pack giveaway, listed as a mention only. Most Solflare Packs posts come from small community accounts with low impressions. The slab idea is marked for legal check because it makes authenticity and vaulting claims. Restock bots, #ad deal accounts, giveaway farms, token shills and carding posts were skipped. Creators already in collector-base.csv or in earlier daily files were excluded.
